subject.title: Proactive messages not visible in session context, causing conversation desynchronization

question: Should successful model-free command cron announcements receive the same destination-session next-turn awareness contract as isolated-agent cron deliveries, with durable transcript mirroring reserved only for paths that require replay visibility?
rationale: The current evidence supports a real gap, but choosing between ephemeral next-turn awareness, durable transcript mirroring, or a shared abstraction changes session semantics, replay behavior, and race handling across multiple proactive-delivery owners.

options.title: Extend target-session awareness
options.body: Route successful command cron announcements through the existing destination-session awareness mechanism and preserve the current isolated-agent distinction between awareness and durable transcript replay.

options.title: Adopt durable transcript mirroring
options.body: Persist successful command announcements into the resolved destination transcript, with explicit dedupe and active-session race protections.

options.title: Define a broader proactive contract first
options.body: Pause implementation until owners document which proactive delivery classes should be ephemeral, durable, or intentionally context-free.

recommendation.title: Extend target-session awareness
recommendation.body: Route successful command cron announcements through the existing destination-session awareness mechanism and preserve the current isolated-agent distinction between awareness and durable transcript replay.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged isolated-cron awareness work is the closest documented implementation boundary for the newly reported command-cron gap.
